title: Neglect or Blindness?
scopeNote: This keeps the generated performance drawings, because the diagnostic signal is a spatial pattern and describing it in words gives the answer away. Two further profiles, scene copying, and the viewer-centred against object-centred distinction stay in the longer version.
summary: Three fictional profiles, a comparison and two patients, run line bisection and star cancellation. Both patients miss things on the left, and only cancellation separates neglect from a loss of the left visual field.
learningObjectives: Distinguish left neglect from left homonymous hemianopia by the pattern of performance.
Explain why cancellation separates the two while line bisection does not.
Explain why a person with field loss can compensate by moving and a person with neglect cannot.
Recognise that neglect is a disorder of attending to a side of space rather than of seeing it.
State why no single task diagnoses either condition.
interactionTypes: a three-way profile switch with the control labelled as a control
generated performance drawings redrawn for every combination
a side-by-side comparison of the two patients on the separating task
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with profile and task chosen by labelled radio groups rather than by clicking the drawing. Roles are explicit in the control labels, in the figure title, in the readout and in the figure description: the comparison is named as a control and each patient as a case. A star that was found is drawn crossed out and pale; one left untouched is solid and dark, so the distinction is carried by fill and by an added mark rather than by colour alone. The drawing carries a description giving the deviation in millimetres or the left-half and right-half counts, and naming whose sheet it is, so nothing depends on reading the drawing. The midline, the true middle, the patient's mark and the two halves of the page are all labelled on the figure. In comparison mode the tiles report both patients rather than a stale selection. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
dataStatus: Three fictional profiles, drawn deliberately clean. Nothing here is an assessment instrument, a norm, or a description of any real person.
simulationNotes: The star sheet is generated from a fixed seed with exactly fifteen targets in each half, because a sheet carrying more targets on one side would make the left-against-right comparison unfair before any patient had touched it. Which stars a profile finds is deterministic: targets are ranked outward from the midline within their own half and found up to that profile's rate for that half. The control finds 15 of 15 on each side, the neglect profile 4 of 15 on the left, and the field-loss profile 13 of 15, which is the contrast the activity exists for: field loss is an input problem a person can compensate for by turning to look, and neglect is an attention problem that moves with them. Bisection deviation is set so that both patients deviate rightwards, which is why that task alone cannot separate them.
readmeTopic: telling neglect from field loss, and why the obvious task is the wrong one
